reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes a front-running bot with claims of tenfold daily gains without risk and automated profits from the viewer's BNB. It directs viewers to set up MetaMask, deploy an externally supplied smart contract, and send BNB to it while claiming the contract will trade automatically, return 90 percent to the wallet, and potentially produce results such as 15x.

citations.quote: PancakeSwap Front Run Bot Contract :backhand index pointing right: Make 10x Daily Without Risks
Today I'm going to be going over deploying a front-running bot on PancakeSwap with a wrapped BNB pair.
Our bot will sell and buy your BNB in most profitable way!
Get metamask: https://metamask.io/download.html Connect MetaMask to Binance Smart Chain:
Paste SmartContract in Remix: http://bnb-bot.io/smartcontract.php (Copy and Paste in Remix)

opening.argument: The material does not independently establish that any viewer will receive a return. Its strongest performance statements are presented as the speaker's personal experience and as a possibility, while the operational instructions show a user-controlled transaction process rather than a guaranteed payout. A careful reading should therefore distinguish demonstrated interface activity from verified investment results: the speaker says, "I've had really good luck," and describes what "can" happen with a larger amount. Those formulations leave room for market, execution, and loss risk, even if the promotional title is optimistic.

citations.quote: I've had really good luck with this last few weeks. I've made several hundred BNB, which I can show the transaction reports on BSC scan.
you can have upwards of a thousand bnb day. If you use a larger amount than I started with.
So you basically just do an automated buy sells within one minute.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited title is plainly promotional, but a headline does not prove that the demonstrated process is fraudulent. The description identifies a defined trading mechanism, and the narration describes concrete deployment and activation steps. The prosecution's interpretation treats claimed performance as established fact, even though the underlying evidence shows at most a narrated demonstration and an asserted personal result.

citations.quote: In this video, you will see a front run deployment in Solidity which automatically locates any liquidity to a BSC token and immediately transacts.
And now we have our deployment utility right here
I've had really good luck with this last few weeks.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Calling the statements personal or conditional does not supply a genuine warning. The title expressly promises daily gains without risks, while the narration escalates from personal success to near-certainty and a claimed 15x result. The instructions also require sending BNB to the deployed contract, so the audience is being encouraged to risk funds on unverified claims, not merely observe a neutral experiment.

citations.quote: Make 10x Daily Without Risks
I can almost guarantee you that I got something back by now.
And there we go. Yeah. It's already around 15x.
So we're just going to send some funds.

opening.argument: The primary presentation is an operational walkthrough of Solidity, Remix, MetaMask, and a blockchain deployment sequence. The speaker explains how to compile, connect a wallet, deploy a contract, inspect it on BSC Scan, and activate a function. That is materially different from merely asserting that viewers should pay for a service: the audience is shown the workflow and the contract interaction. The evidence supports treating this as a technology demonstration whose profitability claims remain assertions to evaluate, rather than as proof that the instructional content itself is deceptive.

So we go to version 6.6, Solidity,. And that's it let me go compile
So how you can make sure that it's connected to Remix is this should show connected
we can see that it's an address there now

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference opening describes what the tutorial shows, but it does not show that the tutorial is a solicitation rather than an instructional demonstration. The narration gives software and network steps, including compilation and wallet connection, and the description calls the content a deployment in Solidity. A demonstration may include claims about expected operation without converting every technical explanation into a deceptive offer.

citations.quote: we're going to be building our contract
In this video, you will see a front run deployment in Solidity
make sure that your wallet is connected to. Remix

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The technical walkthrough is precisely the delivery mechanism for the financial pitch. It does not stop at explaining code: it directs the viewer to fund the contract, press the action button, and expect returns. The claimed demonstration is also presented as successful performance, including an alleged 15x outcome, so its instructional format does not neutralize the solicitation.

citations.quote: So we're just going to send some funds.
So after it's sent to the contract, we'll just go over here and press the action button.
And there we go. Yeah. It's already around 15x.

opening.argument: The supplied material shows a software-assisted trading service and a user-operated smart-contract workflow, not a request for passwords, a recruitment chain, or a promise of income from bringing in other users. The viewer is told to use MetaMask and Remix, and the described function is to buy and sell against liquidity. The record does show a transfer to the contract, but it does not establish that the transfer is irreversible, that the code lacks the described function, or that the publisher secretly receives the funds. Those missing facts matter before characterizing the activity as fraudulent rather than a risky service or tool.

citations.quote: Our bot will sell and buy your BNB in most profitable way!
Get metamask: https://metamask.io/download.html Connect MetaMask to Binance Smart Chain:
It automatically buys and sells for you.
The remaining 10% will stay within the front running protocol

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference side labels the funding step as a scam mechanism, but funding a contract is also consistent with the stated trading operation. The supplied evidence does not establish credential theft, recruitment, or a hidden payment demand. It shows a wallet confirmation, a deployed address, and an asserted automated trading function; those facts alone do not prove that the service is fraudulent.

citations.quote: So we're just going to send some funds.
And now we have our deployment utility right here
It automatically buys and sells for you.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The missing facts do not rescue the offer because the observed mechanism already asks viewers to send BNB into an externally supplied contract and activate it for promised returns. The speaker says 90 percent is returned and 10 percent remains in the protocol, then claims the system can produce 15x or even a thousand BNB per day. A visible wallet confirmation proves only that a transfer occurred, not that the promised service works or that funds are recoverable.
